correctness.rationale: The exact ordered-path Bernoulli survival argument gives protection gain (1-p)F_v(p). A complete Prüfer/center-canonical census at orders 1..8 gives tree counts 1,1,1,2,3,6,11,23. Integer nonnegative transformed coefficients certify a universal winning vertex in all trees of orders at most seven and 21 of the 23 eight-vertex shapes. The remaining two have disjoint rational winner sets and exact polynomial winner-difference factorizations. An independently enumerated rational-site-state sum confirms the gain for both compared interventions. No infinite-tree classification or empirical statement is inferred.

originality.rationale: Earlier ecological graph theory establishes the deterministic C/LCP connectivity measure, patch-importance and link-importance ideas. None of the accessible full primary results or the relevant public-result and web queries showed the specific sharp n=8 classification for global expected-connectivity optimality under independent site survival. The edge-reinforcement analogue changes a different random component and does not imply the node-protection statement. The unread Matisziw–Murray full article and other unlocated reliability results remain acknowledged overlap risks.
residual_risks: Full text of Matisziw and Murray 2009 could not be read despite open-access/preprint and authorized institutional attempts; its exact theorem coverage remains unresolved but its documented approach is deterministic C connectivity change.
Specialized reliability or graph-polynomial literature not retrieved could contain an equivalent stronger classification.
An absence of hits in public search records cannot establish novelty or rule out unpublished work.

value.rationale: Independent habitat loss and one protected patch define an immediately interpretable ecological prioritization problem. The sharp smallest landscape and complete first exceptional shape list give a meaningful nonroutine structural boundary at which protection rankings begin to depend on site survival probability. The result is exact and self-contained, while deliberately avoiding claims of calibrated real-world management advantage or broader graph-family optimality.
